card: This pull request refactors CI environment scripts across 25 platforms to assemble the BITCOIN_CONFIG string using printf instead of multi-line strings. This allows CI maintainers to place explanatory comments adjacent to the specific configuration flags without triggering ShellCheck warnings. The author notes this is a CI documentation and style cleanup with no intended behavioral change. It has no external dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Rebased to resolve merge conflicts, touching 25 setup scripts instead of 26.
evidence: PR description: "This is a CI doc-style-cleanup. `BITCOIN_CONFIG` is a single manually-formatted large string. This is fine, but shellcheck doesn't like when trailing comments are added: `SC2155 -- Declare and assign separately`."
problem: Multi-line string assignments in shell scripts cannot easily contain inline comments without breaking syntax or triggering ShellCheck lint warnings like SC2155, forcing explanatory comments to be separated from the flags they document.

risk.why: A quoting or formatting mistake could cause CI configuration steps to fail or silently omit build flags in CI jobs.

scope_notes: Mechanical refactoring spanning 25 CI setup scripts in ci/test/.
summary: Refactors CI setup environment scripts to format the `BITCOIN_CONFIG` variable using `printf -v BITCOIN_CONFIG "%q "` instead of a multi-line quoted string. This allows configuration comments to be placed directly alongside or above the specific CMake flags they describe.
